review_mode: fresh independent source-only peer; no edits to product code, tests, build, browser, or runtime

verdict_a.finding: The retry clears its old report immediately. Sequence, page-key, and mounted guards prevent late A success/error/finally state writes after a different-URL navigation, newer run, reset, or unmount. The page-keyed visible state also hides A before the navigation effect clears state.
verdict_a.limits: No native or live UI proof exists for D58; the repair report records guarded connected tests and compile only. Same-tab same-URL reload remains indistinguishable because identity is only tab ID + URL, so stale status can survive reload. Cancellation of the injected script is also not provided.

verdict_b.finding: The hook keeps lifecycle ownership local and uses a monotonically increasing run sequence plus mounted/page identity checks. The connected Prepare UI test checks stale success removal on retry failure; deferred hook tests cover A resolve/reject after URL change, overlapping success ordering, reset success, and unmount rejection. Existing red/green/final and compile receipts are consistent with these paths.
verdict_b.gaps: No test executes in this peer lane. The tests mock preparePage, appropriately isolating hook ownership, so they do not prove Chrome injection or live rendering. Reset has only late-success coverage and overlap has only older-success coverage; these leave small error-path assertion gaps, though the same isCurrent guard protects both catch and finally.

existing_runtime_evidence: No native browser acceptance exists for D58 or D57. D58 repair report and completed resource journals record automated runtime red (5 failed, 1 passed), green (6 passed), final (6 passed), and compile success. These are real automated runtime evidence, not native Chrome proof.
scope_assessment: The narrow repair fixes the demonstrated different-page and attempt-order defects without changing the shared tab identity contract. Same-URL reload is an acknowledged pre-existing identity gap shared with Snapshot; expanding this patch to invent document identity here risks a second inconsistent identity mechanism. Track that broader fix at the shared active-tab boundary; do not claim reload coverage.
recommendation: Accept the source repair for the scoped D58 ordering/reset/unmount behaviors, keep native verification open, and retain the explicit same-tab same-URL reload limitation.
